state.assignment_rule: A tier that violates one measured dimension forfeits that class. Remaining tiers compare on aggregate burden: interface breadth, packaged bytes, and recurring per-call price. Catalogue prevails in ties solely for broadly generic surfaces. Companion demands proven auth and release equivalence. Absent complete evidence for every tier, the class reverts to preparation rather than accepting a tier on faith.
state.class_chart: Widget C draws invoice totals as bars, resolves one bar pick, and releases. Adapter form: 3 synchronous entries, 3 failure leaves, one callback under 4 dispatch statutes (serialized dispatch, sealed failure journal, sync reentrant refresh, mid-callback teardown), deeply duplicated frozen values at each border, opaque tokens, safe repeated teardown, 279 lines, 6051-byte bundle ahead of genuine SDK mass. Companion form: render, select, release in typed envelopes, 7 failure leaves, callback-free, frozen bytes with a table per render, safe repeated release, post-release reads expire, pinned 209-byte render plea and 164-byte answer, 360 lines, 20236-byte bundle embedding 11041 shared policy bytes. The workflow succeeds under both; the adapter settles picks in place while the companion bars SDK mass from the audited browser asset. Catalogue sketch: compact vendor-neutral chart entries with a release-pinned renderer, tenable only after charts graduate to platform surface; composing from shipping entries fails on absent canvas and SVG primitives.
state.class_clipboard: Op B shuttles text to and from the device clipboard via an async permission-watched platform entry. Adapter form: 2 async entries, 4 failure leaves, advance permission verdict closing cleanly on denial, declared unordered settling under overlap, callback-free, 156 lines, 2987-byte bundle. Companion form: server pastebin cell in typed envelopes, 9 failure leaves, pinned 106-byte read and 127-byte write pleas, 301 lines, 16768-byte bundle embedding shared policy mass. Decisive gap: server cell never intersects the device cell, hence the companion forfeits the compare-targets dimension for device-clipboard work. Catalogue sketch: 2 generic entries with 4 errors, tenable after live permission-matrix clearance plus a second app's demand.
state.class_storage: Op A retains string keys with string values in a synchronous platform vault ruled by quota and origin. Adapter form: 3 synchronous entries, 3 failure leaves, callback-free, copy-free crossings, an availability gate that leaves the host untouched while shut, 184 lines, 4559-byte bundle. Companion form: 3 async entries, 8 failure leaves, rigorous JSON envelopes pinning a 117-byte get, 132-byte set, and 72-byte answer, destination and credential scrutiny per call, 334 lines, 18360-byte bundle embedding 11041 shared policy bytes. The workflow succeeds under both; companion persistence resides server-side, reframing offline posture, latency, and cross-device span. Catalogue sketch: 3 generic entries with 3 errors, tenable after a further shipped app seeks origin-local persistence.
state.constraints: Outside users number zero, releasing all compatibility claims. Catalogue entry passes solely through compiler acceptance and distribution review; vendor-tied entries never qualify. Outbound traffic honors the destination allowlist, with credentials referenced by environment name and kept out of all logs. Browser views graft solely at the root, while teardown taints handles and sheds tardy callbacks. The second vendor lands with no bespoke compiler alteration.
state.experiment: X-R01-1 grades three integration tiers inside every class following the shared-controls library demonstration: generic catalogue extension, reviewed adapter parcel, companion service. Each class executed a common workflow against a host-injected adapter form and a typed-envelope companion form founded on the shared outbound policy. Launchable browsers never materialized, so native-call confidence derives from cited platform canon awaiting live proof. Six forms span 1638 lines beneath 54 passing legs; all bundles reproduce bit-for-bit.
